title: Ordered vector compositions and proper-interval chains, with dual cohomology
statement:
Let $r\geq0$ and $m=(m_1,\ldots,m_r)\in\mathbf N^r$. For $n\geq0$ let $V_{m,n}$ be the rational vector space with basis the ordered tuples $(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n)$ of nonzero vectors in $\mathbf N^r$ with sum $m$. The empty tuple is a basis vector exactly for $m=0,n=0$. Set $V_{m,n}=0$ for $n<0$. Define
$$\partial_n[\alpha_1|\cdots|\alpha_n]=\sum_{a=1}^{n-1}(-1)^a[\alpha_1|\cdots|\alpha_a+\alpha_{a+1}|\cdots|\alpha_n],$$
with zero differential for $n=0,1$. These maps square to zero. Write $V_m^n{}^*=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Q}(V_{m,n},\mathbf Q)$ with cochain differential $\partial_{n+1}^*$, and define homology and cohomology by the corresponding kernel modulo image [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology].
For $m\ne0$, order $[0,m]=\prod_i\{0,\ldots,m_i\}$ coordinatewise, let $T_m=[0,m]\setminus\{0,m\}$, and let $A(m)_k$ have as basis the strict chains with $k+1$ vertices in $T_m$, with $A(m)_{-1}=\mathbf Q$ on the empty chain and zero terms below $-1$. Its boundary deletes vertices with alternating signs, including the augmentation sending each vertex to $1$. Cumulative partial sums
$$(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n)\longmapsto[\alpha_1<\alpha_1+\alpha_2<\cdots<\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_{n-1}]$$
identify $V_{m,n}$ with $A(m)_{n-2}$ and carry $\partial$ to minus the boundary of $A(m)$, including $n=1$ and the empty chain. Multiplying this map in degree $n$ by $(-1)^n$ gives a chain isomorphism to the chain complex with degree-$n$ term $A(m)_{n-2}$ and its displayed boundary, hence also an isomorphism in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].
For every $m$ and $n\geq0$,
$$\dim_{\mathbf Q}H^n(V_m^*)=\dim_{\mathbf Q}H_n(V_m)=\begin{cases}1&\text{if every }m_i\in\{0,1\}\text{ and }n=\sum_i m_i,\\0&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}$$
In particular $m=0$ gives one copy of $\mathbf Q$ in degree zero, while any coordinate $m_i\geq2$ gives an acyclic complex and acyclic dual. Every term is finite dimensional; if $m\ne0$ it is zero for $n>\sum_i m_i$.

proof.text: Write $s=\sum_i m_i$. In a basis tuple every coordinate of each $\alpha_a$ is between $0$ and $m_i$, so for fixed $n$ the basis is a subset of a finite set of arrays. Also $|\alpha_a|=\sum_i(\alpha_a)_i\geq1$, and $\sum_a|\alpha_a|=s$, so $n\leq s$ for every nonempty basis tuple. Thus every term is finite-dimensional and the asserted upper bound holds. If $m=0$, nonnegativity forces every block to be zero, which is forbidden: only the empty tuple in degree zero remains. Its differential and dual differential vanish. This proves all claims for $m=0$, including $r=0$. Henceforth $m\ne0$, so $r\geq1$.

proof.text: Let $F_n$ be the cumulative-sum map of the statement. For $n\geq2$, its vertices are strictly increasing coordinatewise because each intervening block is nonzero; the first vertex is nonzero and the last is below $m$ because the last block is nonzero. Conversely, from $v_1<\cdots<v_{n-1}$ recover $(v_1,v_2-v_1,\ldots,v_{n-1}-v_{n-2},m-v_{n-1})$. Coordinatewise differences are nonnegative and nonzero, and telescope to $m$. These formulas are mutually inverse. For $n=1$ the unique tuple $(m)$ corresponds to the empty chain in degree $-1$. For $n\leq0$ both spaces are zero. Extending linearly gives isomorphisms $F_n:V_{m,n}\to A(m)_{n-2}$.

proof.text: The alternating boundary $d$ of $A(m)$ squares to zero: for deleted positions $i<j$, the two orders of deletion give signs $(-1)^{i+j-1}$ and $(-1)^{i+j}$; they cancel. For a two-vertex chain the two augmentations cancel, and all lower cases are zero. Merging blocks $a,a+1$ deletes precisely the $a$th cumulative sum, whose zero-based vertex position is $a-1$. Its coefficient in $F_{n-1}\partial_n$ is $(-1)^a$, the negative of its coefficient $(-1)^{a-1}$ in $dF_n$. Thus $F_{n-1}\partial_n=-dF_n$. At $n=2$, explicitly $[\alpha|\beta]\mapsto-[m]$ corresponds to minus the augmentation of $[\alpha]$; at $n=1$ both boundaries are zero. Invertibility of $F$ now gives $\partial^2=0$; precomposition gives $(\partial^*)^2=0$. With $G_n=(-1)^nF_n$, the same identity becomes $G_{n-1}\partial_n=dG_n$. The inverse of $G$ commutes with boundaries by this equation. This proves the stated chain isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology].

proof.text: Reindex the two chain complexes as cochain complexes by $C^j=C_{-j}$. Applying the localization functor of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] to $G$ and its inverse preserves their two inverse identities. Consequently the comparison is an isomorphism in the derived category as asserted.

proof.text: The maps $G$ and $G^{-1}$ send kernels to kernels and images to images, so induce inverse linear maps $H_n(V_m)\cong H_{n-2}(A(m))$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. Apply [lem-sfb-product-chain-proper-interval-homology], with $m\ne0$ and $r\geq1$ established in step 1. A coordinate $m_i\geq2$ makes every group zero. Otherwise the number of coordinates equal to one is $s$, and the sole nonzero interval degree is $s-2$, of dimension one. Since $n-2=s-2$ exactly when $n=s$, this proves the homology dimension formula, including $s=1$ and interval degree $-1$.

proof.text: Put $c_n=\dim V_{m,n}$ and $b_n=\dim\operatorname{im}\partial_n$, with $b_0=0$. The rank-nullity and quotient-dimension identities [lem-weil-pbc-idempotent-charpoly-rank-nullity, lem-trf-vector-space-quotient-dimension], applied to $\partial_n$ and then to its cycle space modulo boundaries, give $\dim H_n(V_m)+b_{n+1}+b_n=c_n$. Boundaries are a subspace of cycles by step 3, and inclusion into $V_{m,n}$ identifies their images linearly. All spaces are finite-dimensional by step 1. For the dual cochain complex, [lem-sfb-linear-dual-dimension-rank] gives term dimension $c_n$ and incoming and outgoing image dimensions respectively $b_n$ and $b_{n+1}$. Applying the same two dimension identities gives $\dim H^n(V_m^*)+b_n+b_{n+1}=c_n$. Reordering the summands and cancelling yields $\dim H^n(V_m^*)=\dim H_n(V_m)$. This includes $n=0$, using the zero incoming map. Step 5 and the $m=0$ case of step 1 give the full displayed formula and the two acyclicity conclusions.
